build_requirements.windows_runtime_needs: Npcap/WinPcap (wpcap.dll) - not installed, driver install out of scope

available_toolchain.host_java: openjdk 17.0.20 (no Java 8; jnetpcap needs Npcap on Windows)

blocking_incompatibilities: CICFlowMeter requires Java 8; neither host nor Kali provides Java 8, and it is not apt-installable on Kali (only Java 11 and Java 25 available).
The bundled Gradle 4.2 wrapper supports only Java 7-9 and cannot run on Java 11/25.
jnetpcap 1.4 (2013) JNI native is very unlikely to load on Java 11/25.
On Windows, jnetpcap additionally requires an Npcap/WinPcap driver that is not installed; installing a system packet-capture driver was out of scope.
Assembling Java 8 + Gradle 4.2 + jnetpcap 1.4 would require manual third-party JDK/Gradle downloads, which would be non-reproducible and against the phase's tooling guidance.
decision: STOP per B2: reproducible Java extractor could not be established, so no same-PCAP dual extraction and no diagnostic parity traffic were performed.
consequence: CASE C persists: empirical same-PCAP extractor parity remains infeasible with available systems. The source/semantic audit (Phase 16E) stands as the strongest available evidence.
